paper.title: RoboNeuron: A Middle-Layer Infrastructure for Agent-Driven Orchestration in Embodied AI
paper.central_claim: RoboNeuron is a middleware between MCP agents and ROS2 that derives agent-callable tools from ROS schemas, offers a direct path and a perception-inference-control (PIC) composition with explicit lifecycle control under one interface, and localizes VLA backend/runtime/acceleration changes inside a stable inference boundary so they can be switched without rewiring.
paper.claim_scope_note: Authors position the evaluation as mechanism validation; the conclusion's 'address practical challenges in scalability, system organization, and backend evolution' exceeds what is measured.

sections_read: IV Experiments A-D (Table I, Figs 3-6 captions)

preliminary_judgment: Written before opening seat totals. Operation: schema parsing turns ROS message definitions into typed, validated tool signatures bound to publishers; long-running modules run as separate processes with start/stop tools; the inference module hides VLA backend, runtime and pruning presets behind a fixed image-in / 6-DoF-delta-out contract. Evidence: Cases I-III are figure-only demonstrations (multi-platform velocity tool, simulated arm, FR3 grasp) with no counts and no named LLM agent; Case IV runs LIBERO (4 suites x 10 tasks x 50 episodes) for OpenVLA-OFT vs RoboNeuron+FastV pruning presets (P25/P50 within about 1.4 points, P75 drops 6.6-7.8) and an OpenVLA latency figure. No RoboNeuron-without-pruning row, so 'middleware does not degrade success' is untested; integration-effort and reuse claims are never measured or compared with ROS2mcp-style bridges or manual wrappers. Initial view: in scope as harness infrastructure; design is clear and reconstructible; evidence for its own claims is mostly existence demonstrations.

evidence.quote: RoboNeuron is a middleware infrastructure that bridges agent tool calling and robot middleware, rather than a planning algorithm or a replacement for existing robot control stacks.
evidence.support_explanation: Center claim is interface infrastructure, not improved agent planning success.

evidence.quote: The architecture decouples semantics from transport by bifurcating the system into a control plane and a data plane.
evidence.support_explanation: Heterogeneous traffic receives distinct execution/lifecycle treatment.

evidence.quote: The system parses ROS message definitions to resolve fields, including nested structures and arrays, and constructs a structured tool argument schema.
evidence.support_explanation: Schema-derived typed tools target manual wrapper drift.

evidence.quote: A dedicated stop tool manages process cleanup, utilizing a bounded wait period before resorting to a forced termination
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit lifecycle semantics; no measured cleanup reliability/race behavior.

evidence.quote: a 6-DoF end-effector delta in position and orientation together with a gripper command.
evidence.support_explanation: Stable semantic action contract; transport vector alone is not arbitrary compatibility.

evidence.quote: the agent can restart the inference module with the new configuration while the perception and control modules continue to run
evidence.support_explanation: Topology-preserving swap, not live same-process instantaneous replacement.

evidence.quote: Each suite contains 10 tasks, and each task is evaluated over 50 episodes.
evidence.support_explanation: LIBERO denominators present for policy-preservation experiment.

evidence.quote: RoboNeuron + P75 98.4 ( \downarrow 0.2 ) 89.8 ( \downarrow 7.8 ) 96.6 ( \downarrow 0.6 ) 89.2 ( \downarrow 6.6 ) 1.58
evidence.support_explanation: Aggressive preset loses success despite stable I/O; no free performance invariance.

evidence.quote: RoboNeuron + P50 99.2 ( \uparrow 0.6 ) 98.4 ( \uparrow 0.8 ) 96.8 ( \downarrow 0.4 ) 94.4 ( \downarrow 1.4 ) 1.17
evidence.support_explanation: Moderate pruning not uniformly neutral; protocol+pruning combined relative to baseline.

evidence.quote: The real-robot study emphasizes feasibility and runtime semantics rather than large-scale statistical performance.
evidence.support_explanation: No physical task denominators, orchestration success rates or reliability measurement.

evidence.quote: Our current prototype also focuses on topic-based capability exposure and a vector action transport format.
evidence.support_explanation: Services/actions and broader interface generality not evaluated.

evidence.quote: Figure 6 reports latency and normalized speedup on an RTX 4090.
evidence.support_explanation: Inference-side latency evaluated separately from task success; no whole-pipeline cost accounting.

evidence.quote: implementations such as ROS2mcpserver [ 23 ] and ROS2mcp [ 24 ] show that ROS capabilities can be connected to such interfaces in practice.
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest bridging systems described but originals/version-specific comparison absent.

evidence.quote: RoboNeuron bridges these ecosystems by deriving agent-callable tools directly from ROS schemas, providing a unified execution abstraction that supports both direct commands and modular composition, and localizing backend, runtime, and acceleration-preset changes within a stable inference boundary.
evidence.support_explanation: 中心主张的三部分。

evidence.quote: RoboNeuron employs schema-based derivation to generate tool signatures directly from ROS message and interface definitions.

evidence.quote: Each long-running module operates as a standalone ROS2 node within a separate OS process, initiated via the spawn method.

evidence.quote: The emphasis of this case is not large-scale task statistics but runtime semantics

assessment.evidence_level_reason: LIBERO closed-loop runs with simulator-checked success and 500 episodes per suite for the stacks run inside the inference boundary; no counted real or agent-in-the-loop trials, no construction-unused setting, so not transfer.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: The prototype exposes ROS messages as typed MCP tools and lets VLA pruning presets be swapped inside a fixed I/O topology; on LIBERO (500 episodes/suite, single run) P25/P50 stay within 1.4 points of the OpenVLA-OFT row and P75 loses 6.6-7.8 points on Object/Long, with 1.03-1.58x speedup.
not_supported_as_stated: middleware itself preserves success (no unpruned RoboNeuron row)
agent-driven orchestration reliability (no named agent, no counts)
assessment.not_claimed: No reproduction; all results are author reports.

G.reason: A real engineering gap (agent tool APIs vs ROS middleware, wrapper drift, backend re-integration) with nearest bridges named (ROS2mcpserver, ROS2mcp, RynnRCP, RoboOS), but the bottleneck's cost is never quantified and the residue over the nearest bridges is asserted, not shown. Anchor 2 (impact/residue incomplete); same standard as 2503.02465 G=2.

M.reason: Schema derivation, control/data split, process isolation and a fixed action contract directly target interface drift and switching cost; no distinguishable prediction about integration effort is tested. Both seats agree.

X.reason: Algorithms 1-2, action contract, lifecycle and PIC data flow reconstructible; driving agent/prompts unspecified, topic-only scope stated. Both seats agree.

measurement.reason: Anchors v2 'criterion exists but denominators incomplete -> 2': the backend-switching contribution has environment-checked LIBERO success with full denominators, while the tool-derivation/lifecycle contributions and the FR3 case have no criterion or counts. Not 0-1 because one of three central contributions is measured with a complete denominator.

causality.reason: No control bears on RoboNeuron's own claims: no middleware on/off, no manual-wrapper or ROS2mcp comparison, no ablation of schema derivation/paths/boundary, and the baseline row's harness status is unstated. Case IV isolates pruning presets (agg:E001), which is evidence about pruning, not the middleware. Above 0 only because the fixed-topology design is demonstrated to support such one-factor preset comparisons.

holdout.reason: No construction-unused schema, robot or backend is tested (pi0 declared but not evaluated); cases appear to be development demonstrations; conclusion-level scalability exceeds the evidence. Between anchor 0 and 2.

statistics.reason: Anchors v2 'no repeats and no failure breakdown -> <=1': each LIBERO configuration is one evaluation without variance or failure decomposition, deltas of 0.2-1.4 points are interpreted without uncertainty, and the cases have no counts.

cost.reason: Per-step latency on RTX 4090 including RoboNeuron overhead and normalized speedup (values in figure); no agent/LLM cost, memory or integration effort. Both seats agree.

son55_value.reason: 完整 HTML 全文（无独立附录）；图 3-6 仅图注可用。

resolutions.reason: Contributions 1 and 3 (typed tool boundary, stable inference boundary) are a delegation of execution from a learned agent to deterministic modules via typed artifacts; sol's direct/PIC partition is contribution 2 and kept as supporting.

C25's load-bearing verify-and-correct loop is absent (son55 itself marks step 3 partial and step 4 missing); argument validation is not solver feedback used to correct the agent. Supporting heterogeneous_decomposition also null (C04 not executed).

Anchor 3/4 needs a sourced bottleneck and a clear residue relative to nearest neighbours; here maintenance/switching costs are not quantified and the shortfalls of ROS2mcp-style bridges are asserted without comparison.

The v2 partial-denominator clause applies: the backend-switching contribution is measured with environment-checked success and complete denominators, the others are not. son55 treats LIBERO as unrelated to the central claim, but switching presets inside the boundary is one of the three stated contributions.

The only controlled variation isolates pruning presets (agg:E001); nothing compares with/without the middleware or against alternative bridges, so the middleware's causal claims have no control. Sol's 2 credits the preset comparison, which supports a claim about pruning.

No schema, platform or backend outside those used to build the prototype is evaluated (pi0 declared only); absence of leakage signs does not make a holdout. son55's 2 rests on the authors' scope limitation, which bears on claim_support, not holdout evidence.
Anchors v2: single evaluation per configuration with no failure breakdown -> <=1; the large per-suite denominator does not provide variance.
K107 (frozen VLA as agent-controlled primitive) is executed without inspect-before-commit; K802 dropped because the toggled factor is a model-side pruning preset, not a harness component.
